what: FinTechathon Topic F judge journey: one scenario through QED's HTTP API on an isolated stack, then every evidence case of that household as the API assembled it, verified offline and against the stack's chain
howToReproduce: cd apps/qed-demo && node scripts/judge-journey.ts (QED_BROWSER_PORT=5491 by default; needs Foundry's anvil in ~/.foundry/bin). A real model: QED_AI_PROVIDER=claude-cli node scripts/judge-journey.ts --real-model, with the owner's approval.

stack.database: a scratch directory, deleted with the stack
stack.prices: synthetic: no market provider was contacted

proposer.note: NOT a model: fixed replies from scripted-double-replies.json.

passkey: A software authenticator (server/softauthn.ts): a P-256 key in memory answering as a platform authenticator would. Not a hardware or platform passkey.

notProduced.why: Not produced on this stack. In presentation mode the synthetic feed refreshes every price every 3 s against a 15 s limit, and the vault prices from its own pools on the chain; nothing reachable through the API makes a price stale. Making one stale needs a change outside this task (for example a labelled, test-stack-only switch that pauses the synthetic feed), or live providers, which this task may not contact. The engine's price-fresh refusal is covered by its unit tests (server/execute.test.ts).

findings: The signed document of an instruction drafted from the scripted test double says "A model (scripted-test-double) drafted this instruction" (server/programs.ts draftedBy): it calls the double a model. The run cases label the call correctly (section 2) and quote the document's sentence with the recorded provider beside it.

When the free funds are below the smallest tranche, the release's tranche rule (chain/vendor roles/treasury.ts) records the impact candidate as 0 and gives the reason "the market is too thin"; the free-funds candidate it records is the binding one. The case shows all five candidates and names those below the minimum.
cannotProve: The proposals came from a scripted test double, not a model. The cases show what QED's controls do with a proposal, including one that follows an injected instruction; they are no evidence of model-directed autonomy or of how a real model resists injection.
In this build nothing a model outputs reaches the chain: a model proposes paper-wallet instructions only; the vault's tranches are decided by the release's deterministic policy code.

The chain is a local Anvil chain (31337) started for this run with valueless test tokens; its transaction hashes are not publicly verifiable and the chain is gone when the stack stops. The case files keep the records; --rpc re-verification needs that chain running.
The passkey was a software authenticator; a signature proves possession of the key, not which device held it.
Paper venues and synthetic prices: no order reached an exchange, no money moved.

A forger who rewrites a case and recomputes every hash makes a file consistent in itself. Changing an amount, a transaction hash, the order of steps, or a case's own refusal is still caught (see tamper); dropping a refusal that a case only lists as related is caught only against an anchor: the root this summary records for each case (verify-evidence.ts --root), once the summary is kept where the forger cannot change it.
No one outside this work has reviewed the code or reproduced this run.
